problem: Pay ranges now appear on all U.S. job postings, and employees are unsure what that means for them.
risk: Without context, visible ranges create anxiety instead of understanding.

parts.label: External & Internal Equity
parts.description: Fair vs. market and vs. peers.

meaning: Market-competitive pay for someone performing well in the role.

distinguishes.label: At midpoint
distinguishes.description: Paid fairly vs. similar roles elsewhere.

distinguishes.label: Below average
distinguishes.description: A negative signal — which midpoint is NOT.

common_confusion: That being at midpoint means underperformance.

prompt: What does being at the midpoint of your range indicate?
expected_response_features: identifies midpoint as market-competitive pay for a fully competent performer
does not interpret midpoint as a performance signal

misconception_predictions.claim: Learners read 'middle of the range' as 'middle of the pack' — a performance judgment rather than a market anchor.
misconception_predictions.source: distinction p004 common_confusion; segment × objective entry pending audience model
misconception_predictions.feedback: Midpoint isn't a performance rating — it's the market anchor for a fully competent performer in the role.

feedback_incorrect: Midpoint describes your pay's position against the market, not your performance.
source_reference: Brunswick pay-transparency source deck, ranges section

purpose: See your full compensation beyond base pay.

takeaway: Pay transparency gives you information to have informed conversations.
call_to_action: Start with your manager or HR Business Partner.
